sources.title: French royal biography: education, 1993 doctorate and July 1999 accession
sources.findings: Read relevant French official biography paragraphs: Rabat August 21, 1963; 1985 licence in law; 1988 Brussels traineeship with Jacques Delors; October 29, 1993 Nice–Sophia Antipolis law doctorate on EEC–Maghreb cooperation. French July 1988 wording is diplôme des études supérieures du doctorat en droit public, not independently verified completion of an additional doctorate. July 23, 1999 accession follows Hassan II death; July 30 first Throne Day address is a distinct event.

sources.title: English royal biography, compared with French wording and honorary degree
sources.findings: Read English official biography and degree/award entries. It calls the July 1988 qualification a doctorate, unlike the more specific French wording; do not count a second doctorate. Both agree on 1985 law degree and 1993 Nice doctorate. English entry explicitly records George Washington University honorary doctorate June 22, 2000. Official institutional wording is attributed biographical evidence, not independent authentication of original diplomas or birth documents. Decorative praise is not reproduced.

sources.title: 2011 Constitution: royal, religious, military and appointment powers
sources.findings: Read relevant official 2011 Constitution sections: articles 41 and 42 separate religious and head-of-state functions; article 47 appointment from the party leading House of Representatives elections; article 48 council presidency; article 53 armed-forces supreme command. Royal decree dated July 29, 2011 differs from July 1 referendum and July 30 official-gazette issue. No assertion the constitution removed substantive royal authority or made king and head of government identical.

sources.title: Constitutional referendum chronology: 1 July 2011
sources.findings: Read official constitutional referendum chronology explicitly listing July 1, 2011. It supports referendum date; promulgation comes from the official text, and political context from Brookings. Do not treat listing of a referendum as an independent audit of turnout, result percentages or electoral fairness.

sources.title: Analysis of reforms, infrastructure, inequality and political power, 2020
sources.findings: Read substantive sections of Brookings 2020 analysis on reforms, family law, political authority, rural–urban differences and repression. Family-law change in 2004 and 2011 reform context are historical; analytic judgments are attributed, not presented as unanimous findings or fresh 2026 measurements. No causal claim that the king alone built every project, no current poverty/unemployment statistics and no forecast treated as an accomplished event.

sources.title: World Report 2026: events of 2025, rights concerns and family-code limitations
sources.findings: Read Human Rights Watch World Report 2026 country chapter explicitly labelled Events of 2025: criticism of repression of protesters/critics and family-code inequalities and exceptions. Attribute rights assessments to HRW; publication year does not turn described 2025 events into 2026 events. Discussion of subsequent family-code proposals is historical as of the report; no claim to have audited current November 2026 enactment status, all court files or each allegation.

sources.title: INDH impact study: 18 May 2005 announcement, implementation and evaluation framework
sources.findings: Read relevant background/methodology paragraphs of World Bank-hosted INDH impact study: royal announcement May 18, 2005, main programme launch September 2005, phases and targeted services. Evaluation uses 2008/2011/2013 surveys with design restrictions. Canonical text only adopts launch and programme scope; no nationwide poverty-elimination claim, causal effect estimate or proof every beneficiary target was met.

sources.title: 28th summit concludes with Morocco admission and royal address, 31 January 2017
sources.findings: Read AU January 31, 2017 closing communiqué documenting Morocco admission/readmission at the 28th summit and actual address by Mohammed VI. Use month precision for the membership milestone rather than equating communiqué date and decision date. Morocco joining the AU/restoring participation in the pan-African institutional framework does not establish a final Western Sahara settlement. Do not infer later incumbencies of AU officials from this historical release.

sources.title: Tangier–Kenitra high-speed railway inauguration, 15 November 2018
sources.findings: Read SYSTRA November 15, 2018 inauguration report: king and Emmanuel Macron aboard Al Boraq, new Tangier–Kenitra high-speed infrastructure and services continuing via Rabat to Casablanca. Distinguish new high-speed section from whole service route. Contractor is a project participant; its commercial praise, passenger forecasts and claimed budget performance are not independent audited outcomes. No specific route-length figure adopted where other reports differ.

sources.publisher: Head of Government — Kingdom of Morocco
sources.title: King appoints Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri to form government, 29 September 2026
sources.findings: Read official September 29, 2026 completed audience and appointment statement: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, coordinator of PAM collective leadership, appointed head of government and tasked with forming it under article 47. Do not equate designation with already completed cabinet, parliamentary confidence or replacement of the monarch. Generic party-leader description avoids falsely asserting sole presidency of collective leadership.

sources.publisher: Head of Government — Kingdom of Morocco
sources.title: Completed royal audience with head of government tasked with formation, 14 October 2026
sources.findings: Read October 14, 2026 official completed audience at Rabat Royal Palace, with head of government tasked with formation reporting progress. This is an actual event, not a planned audience or evidence the cabinet had already been sworn in that day. Wishes for successful government action are not achieved policy outcomes.

sources.title: New ministers sworn before the king on 16 October, reported 17 October 2026
sources.findings: Read Le Monde October 17, 2026 headline, substantive lead and body rendered by search tool despite subscriber/gift UI: 32 ministers sworn before the king on Friday October 16. Canonical text uses the occurrence/date only, without minister-by-minister claims, a claim of equal representation or completed confidence vote. The article describes handover/next parliamentary steps separately; no schedule is converted into a completed event.

sources.title: Working session in Rabat on Western Sahara, 4 November 2026; party positions attributed
sources.findings: Read Royal Office/MAP November 4, 2026 statement identifying actual king-chaired working session at Rabat Royal Palace and participants including El Mansouri. Western Sahara sovereignty, autonomy, ceasefire and mission assessments are positions of a party to the dispute. Canonical text uses meeting and attributed policy position, not the statement as proof of final internationally settled sovereignty or a fully independently audited UN mission-closure chronology.
